年.meaning: Under a <part>diving board</part> stands a <part>drying rack</part>. Every summer you hang your towel on it after the first dive, and every summer the towel is a little more faded. Count the faded towels and you know how many have passed, one per <kanji>year</kanji>.
年.on: Once a year the bed li<sound>nen</sound> goes out on the rack too, and comes back smelling of pool.
年.kun: Every year a <sound>to</sound>tem pole carver adds one more <sound>shee</sound>p to the pole.

朝.meaning: The <part>moon</part> works the night shift at a street stall. When the first yawning customers turn up in their pyjamas, it hands each one a hot <part>kebab</part>, then pulls down the shutter and goes to bed. Kebabs for breakfast: it must be <kanji>morning</kanji>.
朝.on: Before it leaves, the moon puts on a sparkly <sound>cho</sound>ker so no customer can miss it.
朝.kun: A customer yawns '<sound>Ah</sound>…' and asks for <sound>sa</sound>rdines on the side.

外.meaning: One <part>evening</part>, someone leaves the garden <part>faucet</part> running. Nobody indoors notices. By morning the lawn is a pond and ducks have moved in. That's what happens when you forget about things <kanji>outside</kanji>.
外.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads you out to the faucet in the dark and turns it off with its nose.
外.kun: Out on the flooded lawn a <sound>so</sound>fa bobs in the water, and a <sound>to</sound>tem pole floats past.

王.meaning: Three planks stacked up like a tall throne, one post nailed straight through the middle of them. Whoever sits on the top plank, feet on the bottom one and elbows on the middle, gives the orders. He's the <kanji>king</kanji>.
王.on: The king's throne is carved from one huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and acorns keep dropping on his crown.

国.meaning: Peer into the <part>jewel</part> locked in a glass <part>cage</part> at the museum, and you see tiny fields, tiny towns and tiny people waving tiny flags inside it. Visitors queue for hours to look. A whole <kanji>country</kanji> lives inside that stone.
国.on: A <sound>cock</sound>atoo sits on top of the cage and screams at anyone who taps the glass.
国.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo guards the cage door and pecks every visitor on the k<sound>nee</sound>.

金.meaning: A <part>king</part> hides under an <part>umbrella</part>, two little <part>horns</part> of nuggets tucked in beside him. It isn't raining. He just doesn't want anyone to see the shine of his <kanji>gold</kanji>.
金.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives down and snatches a nugget from right under the umbrella.
金.kun: The king stuffs his gold into a <sound>ca</sound>r boot and a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t, then goes shopping with it: money.
